geo:GSE327941.overall_design: We profiled recurrent GBM cells, tumor-infiltrating immune cells, and paired peripheral blood immune cells from CD34+ hematopoietic stem cellâreconstituted humanized NOG-EXL mice implanted with JX14P-RT tumors. For tumor cell analysis, we analyzed EGFP+ tumor cells from three humanized mice and two naive mice. For immune cell analysis, we analyzed tumor-infiltrating immune cells and paired peripheral blood immune cells from three humanized mice. Single-cell suspensions enriched for CD45+ immune cells or EGFP+ tumor cells by cell sorting were subjected to scRNA-seq using the 10x Genomics single-cell platform. We generated a 10x Genomics Gene Expression library together with a paired Antibody Capture library containing both HTO and ADT features. HTO was used for sample multiplexing, and HTO-to-sample correspondence is provided in the supplementary file HTO_samples.csv. ADT data were included in the integrated dataset. geo:GSE333876.title: Epigenetic landscape, key transcriptional regulators, and in vivo identification of human Tr1 cells [ATAC-seq]
geo:GSE333876.study_title: Epigenetic landscape, key transcriptional regulators, and in vivo identification of human Tr1 cells [ATAC-seq]
geo:GSE333876.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Genome binding/occupancy profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE333876.description: Type 1 regulatory T (Tr1) cells are CD4+ T cells with immunoregulatory function, which are induced from mature peripheral CD4+ T cells in response to persistent extra-thymic antigens. The role of human Tr1 cells in disease is not completely understood, because transcription factors that regulate their antigen-driven differentiation are not known, and there is lack of consensus on how to best identify them in the tissue, where antigen interactions occur. Here, we leveraged comprehensive bulk and single-cell (sc) transcriptomic, epigenomic, and TCR repertoire profiling of human antigen-induced Tr1 cells, complemented with CRISPR-based functional genomics, to uncover the role of transcription factors IRF4, BATF and MAF in human Tr1 cell differentiation and function. In addition, we identify a Tr1 cell transcriptional signature that can reveal Tr1-like cells in sc-RNA-seq datasets of peripheral blood CD4+ T cells of patients treated with Tr1 therapy, and within tumor-resident CD4+ T cells in patients with clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, triple-negative breast cancer, and colorectal cancer. These data enable further development of Tr1 therapies and Tr1-targeting treatments, and provide new insights into human Tr1 cell biology.

geo:GSE346050.title: MAPK signaling links BRD2 chromatin occupancy to PI3K/AKT inhibitor sensitivity [KO_RNA]
geo:GSE346050.study_title: MAPK signaling links BRD2 chromatin occupancy to PI3K/AKT inhibitor sensitivity [KO_RNA]
geo:GSE346050.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE346050.description: Bromodomain and extra-terminal (BET) proteins, BRD2, BRD3, BRD4, and BRDT, are acetyl-lysine readers that couple histone acetylation to transcriptional output by recruiting elongation and transcription factor complexes to chromatin. BET proteins are promising therapeutic targets, but the functions of individual family members remain incompletely understood. Here we identify BRD2 as a co-targetable vulnerability with PI3K/AKT inhibition in breast cancer. Pan-BET inhibition and BRD2 knockout each synergized with PI3K pathway inhibitors in breast cancer cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and in vivo. BRD2 knockout impaired proliferation of triple-negative breast cancer cells and transcriptionally upregulated key signaling and stress response pathways, including the DNA damage response. Mechanistically, BRD2 is phosphorylated at Serine 37 (Ser37) by the mitogen- and stress-activated kinases MSK and RSK, and Ser37 phosphorylation is required for BRD2 chromatin binding and reader function. Together, these findings identify BRD2 as a phosphorylation-dependent, co-targetable vulnerability in PI3K pathway-inhibited breast cancer.

geo:GSE346343.title: Single-Cell Landscape of Lymphoid and Myeloid Heterogeneity Across Type-Stratified Craniofacial Lesions in Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia
geo:GSE346343.study_title: Single-Cell Landscape of Lymphoid and Myeloid Heterogeneity Across Type-Stratified Craniofacial Lesions in Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia
geo:GSE346343.notes: resp_score=0; gdstype=Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
geo:GSE346343.description: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia (POFD) is a mosaic skeletal disorder driven by somatic GNAS mutations that constitutively activate Gsα-cAMP signaling, producing fibro-osseous craniofacial deformities. POFD lesions are histologically classified into three subtypes—Type I (connective-tissue predominant), Type II (cancellous-bone predominant), and Type III (sclerotic-bone predominant)—yet the immune microenvironment across these categories remains undefined. This study aims to dissect lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity and inter-cellular communication networks among distinct POFD histological categories.
